title: A treasury policy, spoken into existence
description: Preplanned text utterances interpreted by a real Codex agent over MCP. Not a microphone test.

cues.text: Show me ETH’s price and our grant vault.
cues.note: Two persistent objects, fetched data and source timestamps.
This now refers to the ETH price object.

cues.text: If this drops below three thousand dollars, pause spending from the grant vault.
Only if the observation is fresh, no older than sixty seconds. And skip it if the vault is already paused.

cues.note: Frame the graph and readable sentence.
Deliberately ambiguous: there are threshold, freshness and paused-state conditions. Highlight candidates and ask for clarification.

cues.text: Set the threshold to one dollar so this is a false-condition test. Run that version.
cues.note: A deliberately false threshold is independent of market movement.

cues.text: Raise the threshold above the current price so we can test the pause.
cues.note: Uses the observed price rather than a hardcoded test threshold.
Freeze revision; return a run ID; wait for verified execution evidence.

cues.text: Actually, make the draft threshold one dollar again. Keep the version already running unchanged.
cues.note: A planned revision during asynchronous execution; submitted after the run tool returns, before receipt polling.

cues.text: Explain what happened in that last run. Show its frozen threshold, the transaction receipt, and a fresh vault read.
cues.note: Inspect chain evidence, not the changed draft.

cues.text: Raise the draft threshold above the current price and run it again. Explain why spending stays paused without a second pause action.
